# syscall

Types from the Go package `syscall` (a library PocketBase builds on), as JavaScript sees them: they turn up as values of [PocketBase's types](/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase) and of hook events.

## syscall.Credential

Credential holds user and group identities to be assumed
by a child process started by `StartProcess`.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `uid` | <code>number // User ID.</code> |  |
| `gid` | <code>number // Group ID.</code> |  |
| `groups` | <code>Array&lt;number&gt; // Supplementary group IDs.</code> |  |
| `noSetGroups` | <code>boolean // If true, don&#39;t set supplementary groups</code> |  |

## syscall.SysProcAttr

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `chroot` | <code>string // Chroot.</code> |  |
| `credential?` | <code><a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/syscall#syscallcredential">Credential</a> // <a href="/docs/reference/javascript/pocketbase/syscall#syscallcredential">Credential</a>.</code> |  |
| `ptrace` | <code>boolean // Enable tracing.</code> |  |
| `setsid` | <code>boolean // Create session.</code> |  |
| `setpgid` | <code>boolean</code> | Setpgid sets the process group ID of the child to Pgid, or, if Pgid == 0, to the new child's process ID. |
| `setctty` | <code>boolean</code> | Setctty sets the controlling terminal of the child to file descriptor Ctty. Ctty must be a descriptor number in the child process: an index into ProcAttr.Files. This is only meaningful if Setsid is true. |
| `noctty` | <code>boolean // Detach fd 0 from controlling terminal</code> |  |
| `ctty` | <code>number // Controlling TTY fd</code> |  |
| `foreground` | <code>boolean</code> | Foreground places the child process group in the foreground. This implies Setpgid. The Ctty field must be set to the descriptor of the controlling TTY. Unlike Setctty, in this case Ctty must be a descriptor number in the parent process. |
| `pgid` | <code>number // Child&#39;s process group ID if Setpgid.</code> |  |

## syscall.RawConn

A RawConn is a raw network connection.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `control()` | <code>(f: (fd: number) =&gt; void): void</code> | Control invokes f on the underlying connection's file descriptor or handle. The file descriptor fd is guaranteed to remain valid while f executes but not after f returns. |
| `read()` | <code>(f: (fd: number) =&gt; boolean): void</code> | Read invokes f on the underlying connection's file descriptor or handle; f is expected to try to read from the file descriptor. If f returns true, Read returns. Otherwise Read blocks waiting for the connection to be ready for reading and tries again repeatedly. The file descriptor is guaranteed to remain valid while f executes but not after f returns. |
| `write()` | <code>(f: (fd: number) =&gt; boolean): void</code> | Write is like Read but for writing. |

## syscall.Errno

An Errno is an unsigned number describing an error condition.
It implements the error interface. The zero Errno is by convention
a non-error, so code to convert from Errno to error should use:

```
	err = nil
	if errno != 0 {
		err = errno
	}
```

Errno values can be tested against error values using `errors.is`.
For example:

```
	_, _, err := syscall.Syscall(...)
	if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) ...
```

Has everything <code>Number</code> has.

| Member | Type | |
|---|---|---|
| `error()` | <code>(): string</code> |  |
| `is()` | <code>(target: Error): boolean</code> |  |
| `temporary()` | <code>(): boolean</code> |  |
| `timeout()` | <code>(): boolean</code> |  |
